findings.title: Unparenthesized OR conditions in getBaseConditions break SQL operator precedence when combined with AND
findings.body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` (line 173), `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` (line 206), and `buildFilterConditions` for `eventTypeId` (line 106) produce `Prisma.Sql` fragments with a top-level `OR` that is not wrapped in outer parentheses (for example, `(("teamId" = $1) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)) OR (("userId" = ANY($2)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false))`). When both `authConditions` and `filterConditions` are present, `getBaseConditions()` wraps each in parentheses (`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})`), but when `filterConditions` is `null` (line 74-75), it returns `authConditions` directly without outer parentheses. Because `AND` has higher precedence than `OR` in SQL, any caller that interpolates `${baseConditions}` (or `${authConditions}` / `${filterConditions}`) into a `WHERE` clause alongside other conditions such as date bounds or status checks (e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ...`) will only apply the additional `AND` predicates to one branch of the `OR`, leaking rows that do not match the other filters.

findings.title: Fallback branch in getBaseConditions returns filterConditions without authorization if authConditions is falsy
findings.body: In `getBaseConditions()`, lines 76-77 contain `else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }`. While `getAuthorizationConditions()` currently always returns a truthy `Prisma.Sql`, if it is ever changed to return `null`/`undefined` on failure (matching `getFilterConditions()`), `getBaseConditions()` would silently return `filterConditions` alone with no authorization predicate instead of `NOTHING_CONDITION`. If `authConditions` is not present, `getBaseConditions()` should always return `NOTHING_CONDITION`.
